children: shares jumped in premarket trading Friday after CEO, president and chairman Ryan Cohen made a major open-market purchase of the retailer's stock, giving investors a fresh insider-confidence signal just days after the company reported sharply higher profitability despite another drop in sales.

Cohen acquired 1 million Class A shares for roughly $20.38 million across multiple transactions, paying between $20.0199 and $20.4699 per share. The weighted-average purchase price was $20.3759, lifting his direct ownership to 39.3 million shares. GameStop stock rose 3.5% in premarket trading following the disclosure.

GameStop, once primarily a video-game retailer, has been reshaping its business around collectibles, cost reductions and a broader capital-allocation strategy. The company has also deployed significant capital into investments including eBay stock and Bitcoin, making its balance sheet increasingly important to the investment thesis.

Cohen's purchase comes just three days after GameStop reported second-quarter operating income of $160.2 million, the highest for any second quarter in company history. Net income rose to $298.7 million from $168.6 million a year earlier, while adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $174 million.

The underlying sales picture remains more complicated. Revenue fell to $790.2 million from $972.2 million, partly because of store closures, the divestiture of GameStop's France operations and a difficult comparison with last year's Nintendo Switch 2 launch. Collectibles provided the standout growth engine, with sales surging 57% to $356.3 million and representing 45.1% of quarterly revenue.

Cohen's multimillion-dollar purchase strengthens the alignment between management and shareholders, but investors still need evidence that GameStop's improving profitability can persist as traditional retail sales shrink.

The critical numbers are collectibles growth, operating margins and GameStop's new fiscal-2026 adjusted EBITDA target of more than $650 million. Investors should also closely watch capital allocation: GameStop held about $5.4 billion in cash, securities and digital assets plus a $4.9 billion eBay stake at quarter-end, while long-term debt was reduced to roughly $2.8 billion following recent convertible-note exchanges.

If collectibles growth and cost discipline keep lifting earnings despite weaker revenue, Cohen's purchase could look increasingly significant. A renewed deterioration in operating results or losses on GameStop's large outside investments would weaken that case.

title: Ryan Cohen Doubles Down on GameStop Stock
